candidateAudit.text: Mariahilfer Kirche, Wien — Почитаемый образ «Марияхильф» был подарен церкви в 1660 году. Это копия знаменитой Мадонны с Младенцем Лукаса Кранаха Старшего, созданной около 1537 года. К образу потянулись паломники, и церковь расширили. В 1758 году его поместили на главный алтарь. Образ дал имя церкви и району Мариахильф. #Mariahilf #Wien #Geschichte #Kunst #Kirche

candidateAudit.title: 2026 kommen in Wien 100 von 240 Taufbewerbern aus der islamischen Welt. Das sagt der Priester Christoph Matyssek, und viele der Taufbewerber zahlen für ihre Taufe einen sehr hohen
candidateAudit.text: 2026 kommen in Wien 100 von 240 Taufbewerbern aus der islamischen Welt. Das sagt der Priester Christoph Matyssek, und viele der Taufbewerber zahlen für ihre Taufe einen sehr hohen Preis. Matyssek betreut in Wien die afghanisch-persische katholische Gemeinde. Manche dort haben im Iran Christen getroffen, die ihnen rieten, die Bibel zu lesen. Andere wiederum erzählen von Heilungen nach einem Gebet zu Jesus. Fast alle können danach nicht mehr zu ihren Familien zurück. Im Iran gelten Konvertiten als Abtrünnige, und viele sitzen dort jahrelang im Gefängnis. Auch hier müssen sie wachsam bleiben, sagt Matyssek, die Iraner, weil ihr Geheimdienst aktiv ist, und die Kurden wegen des Drucks ihrer Familienclans. Trotzdem kommen sie, denn der Glaube ist für sie der Schatz, für den es sich lohnt, alles zu verkaufen, so nennt es Jesus im Gleichnis vom Schatz im Acker. Wie selbstverständlich ist dir dein Glaube, wenn du das hörst? candidateAudit.text: 🇮🇹🍰 PASTIERA NAPOLETANA – MEHR ALS EIN DESSERT, EIN STÜCK GESCHICHTE! ❤️ 😍 Wusstest du, dass hinter diesem italienischen Meisterwerk eine jahrhundertealte Geschichte steckt? 🌊 Einer neapolitanischen Legende nach beginnt alles mit der wunderschönen Sirene Partenope, die die Menschen im Golf von Neapel mit ihrem Gesang verzauberte. Als Dank schenkten ihr die Menschen sieben kostbare Zutaten – darunter Weizen, Ricotta, Eier und Orangenblütenwasser. Aus diesen Geschenken soll die erste Pastiera entstanden sein. ✨ ⛪ Über die Jahrhunderte wurde die Pastiera zu einem Symbol der neapolitanischen Ostertradition. Besonders die Nonnen des Klosters San Gregorio Armeno waren für ihre Zubereitung berühmt. 🥧 Zarter Mürbeteig, cremiger Ricotta, gekochter Weizen und der unverwechselbare Duft von Orangenblüten ... ❤️ Bei I Fratelli Pulcinella bringen wir dieses Stück neapolitanischer Kultur direkt nach Wien! Denn für uns ist die Pastiera nicht einfach nur ein Kuchen. SIE IST HEIMAT. SIE IST FAMILIE. SIE IST NAPOLI. 🇮🇹❤️ 📍 I Fratelli Pulcinella 📍 Wienerbergstraße 11 – Twin Towers, 1100 Wien 👇 HAST DU SCHON EINMAL ECHTE NEAPOLITANISCHE PASTIERA PROBIERT? 🤤 Schreib es in die Kommentare und markiere jemanden, der dieses Dessert unbedingt probieren muss! ❤️ #PastieraNapoletana #FratelliPulcinella #Napoli #WienFood #ViennaFood

candidateAudit.text: With the next exhibition (opening tonight!) we again offer an extended program: Slide through all dates, join us for one of the curator's tours or save the first dates for 2027! 🌳 There are also a few last spots for the workshop with Beatrice Tulagan (19 Nov, 14:00!) – register via mail to ail@uni-ak.ac.at 🌳 AIL, Otto Wagner Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 (closed on public holidays, free entry) ail.angewandte.at About the exhibition 'Future on Trial. Between Unruly Evidence and Unfinished Climate Justice’: Contributions by: adO/Aptive, Beatrice Tulagan, Eline Benjaminsen, Elias Kimaiyo, Forensic Architecture, Jonas Staal, Paolo Cirio, Prin Rodriguez, Radha D’Souza, Valentino Skarwan Curators: Adriano Vinca, Camille Belmin, Elisabeth Falkensteiner Expert and scientific support: Inga Menke, Jameela Joy Reyes, Krishna Ariola, Michaela Krömer, Nicholas Petkov The engagement with climate justice reveals a complex field of perspectives across multiple temporalities, geographies, and forms of knowledge. In this context, environmental destruction is entangled with economic interests, the uneven distribution of risks and responsibilities, colonial continuities, imperialist power relations, and geological deep time. The exhibition Future on Trial. Between Unruly Evidence and Unfinished Climate Justice moves between two conceptions of justice. One that is produced and negotiated in courtrooms through scientific and legal evidence, data, and visual investigations, and another that understands justice as an unfinished, collective process, grounded

candidateAudit.text: Star anise, cinnamon, and charred ginger—the very spices that define the Christmas season are the heart and soul of authentic Hanoi Phở Bò. Slow-simmered for hours for a clear, deeply aromatic broth without heavy sweetness, poured steaming hot over silky flat rice noodles and tender beef. Step out of the chilly Vienna winter and soak up the festive warmth at VIN. 📍 Währinger Straße 137, 1180 Wien ⏰ Tue – Fri: 11:30 – 15:30 & 17:00 – 22:00 | Sat & Sun: 11:30 – 22:00 | Mon: Closed Sternanis, Zimt und gerösteter Ingwer – genau jene Gewürze, die wir an der Weihnachtszeit so lieben, bilden das Herzstück unseres authentischen Phở Bò nach Hanoi-Art. Stundenlang langsam geköchelt für eine klare, tiefwürzige Brühe ganz ohne künstliche Süße, serviert mit seidigen Reisbandnudeln und zartem Rindfleisch. Entfliehe der vorweihnachtlichen Kälte und wärme dich bei uns im VIN auf. 📍 Währinger Straße 137, 1180 Wien ⏰ Di – Fr: 11:30 – 15:30 & 17:00 – 22:00 | Sa & So: 11:30 – 22:00 | Mo: Ruhetag

candidateAudit.title: Er hat Niki Lauda nach seinem Unfall zurück an die Spitze geholfen. Und er hat mit meinem Opa zusammengearbeitet. 🏎️ Die Rede ist von Willi Dungl, Masseur, Trainer und einer der P
candidateAudit.text: Er hat Niki Lauda nach seinem Unfall zurück an die Spitze geholfen. Und er hat mit meinem Opa zusammengearbeitet. 🏎️ Die Rede ist von Willi Dungl, Masseur, Trainer und einer der Pioniere der ganzheitlichen Gesundheitspflege in Österreich. Mein Opa hat damals schon auf Bio und das volle Korn gesetzt, als das in der Branche noch kaum jemand gemacht hat. Eigene Filialen in Wien gab es noch nicht, unser Brot stand im Regal von Reformhäusern und Drogerien. Gekauft haben es vor allem Menschen, die sich bewusst mit Ernährung beschäftigt haben. An der Grundidee hat sich bis heute wenig geändert: Wir backen mit dem vollen Korn samt Keimling, mit regionalen Bio-Zutaten, und wir lassen unseren Teigen Zeit. Nur das Regal in der Drogerie haben wir mittlerweile gegen eigene Filialen in Wien und im Burgenland und einen Onlineshop für ganz Österreich getauscht. Wer von euch kennt den Namen Willi Dungl noch? Euer Oliver 🌾 #GradwohlBackstube #Familiengeschichte #BioPionier #Vollkorn #Tradition

candidateAudit.text: Have you been waiting for a sign to start your next crafting project? candidateAudit.text: #Neu im Sortiment aus #Kanada #BlackApron Beef Black Apron Beef showcases some of the best the Canada has to offer. Raised with the same traditional values used in our butcher shops, our Angus cattle roam open pastures on Canadian ranches and are raised without the use of added growth hormones and steroids. Raised on barley based feed and prairie grass, our beef has a taste like no other. – a taste that is a true result of being ‘made in Canada’. Aged for a minimum of 14 days Black Apron beef is 100% Canadian Angus bringing the taste of western Canadian tradition to your kitchen. Our beef is the perfect blank canvas for mouth-watering culinary creations that no carnivore will be able to resist.

candidateAudit.text: The next exhibition opening is coming up – come join us! With a Live Set by Rudi Gier gmorrk and DJ Set by Oko Oko a.made.up.reality Welcome by Gerhild Steinbuch (Executive Board AIL), the curatorial team, and inspiration circle. Intervention by Jameela Joy Reyes and Nicholas Petkov Rudi Gier is a project by sound artist Evamaria Müller. In Rudi Gier's soundscapes, sonic dimensions of our environment form fleeting relationships that resist any categorization. Tactile impulses, geophonic shifts, and synthetic textures combine into a fabric in which organic forms break apart and continually reassemble in new ways. Oko Oko’s sets navigate between experimental sounds and dancefloor-oriented aesthetics. The selection takes detours via ambient, leftfield, and outsider approaches: rhythmic noise and low-fi grooves. About the exhibition: The engagement with climate justice reveals a complex field of perspectives across multiple temporalities, geographies, and forms of knowledge. The exhibition moves between two conceptions of justice. One that is produced and negotiated in courtrooms through scientific and legal evidence, data, and visual investigations, and another that understands justice as an unfinished, collective process, grounded in Indigenous knowledge, queer ecology, multispecies perspectives, and activism. Through a dialogue between artistic practices and scientific experts in the field of climate litigation, the exhibition opens up a space between evidence and uncertainty, accusation and repair, institutional accountability and collective imagination. candidateAudit.title: Neue Ausstellung in der kunsthallewien 🎬 Mit #OvertListening präsentiert die Kunsthalle Wien die erste institutionelle Einzelausstellung der Künstlerin Tiffany Sia in Österreich.
candidateAudit.text: Neue Ausstellung in der kunsthallewien 🎬 Mit #OvertListening präsentiert die Kunsthalle Wien die erste institutionelle Einzelausstellung der Künstlerin Tiffany Sia in Österreich. Die Ausstellung bewegt sich zwischen Militärbunkern, Museumsdisplay und verlassenen Küsten und verwebt Landschaften mit den Klängen von Radioübertragungen und MilitärübungenIm – im Zentrum steht dabei ein neuer Film über die Kinmen-Inseln vor der Küste Taiwans. 📍Kunsthalle Wien 🎥 Tiffany Sia – Overt Listening 🗓️ bis So., 24.01.2027 🔴 #MuseumsQuartier New exhibition at kunsthallewien 🎬 With #OvertListening, the Kunsthalle Wien presents artist Tiffany Sia’s first institutional solo exhibition in Austria. The exhibition moves between military bunkers, museum displays, and deserted coastlines, interweaving landscapes with the sounds of radio broadcasts and military exercises—at its heart is a new film about the Kinmen Islands off the coast of Taiwan.

candidateAudit.text: Baguette kann auch richtig kernig sein! 🥖🌾 Wer sagt, dass Baguette immer klassisch sein muss? Unser BIO Kornbaguette bringt Abwechslung auf den Jausentisch. Feine Aromen. Echtes Handwerk. 🌻 Bei unserem BIO Kornbaguette steckt der Geschmack in vielen kleinen Details. Geröstete Sonnenblumenkerne und Leinsamen sorgen für kräftige, nussige Noten. Ein Zusammenspiel, das Erfahrung und Fingerspitzengefühl verlangt. Kernig im Biss, saftig im Inneren. 🤎 Eine wunderbar saftige Krume trifft auf den herzhaften Geschmack von Sonnenblumenkernen, Leinsamen und Schrot. Mit viel Sorgfalt und handwerklichem Können entsteht ein Baguette mit hohem Ballaststoffgehalt, das mit jedem Bissen begeistert. Wäre das etwas für deine nächste Jause? 🥖

candidateAudit.title: Sari Schorr kehrt nach Europa zurück – und sie kommt nicht leise. In diesem Herbst bringt die New Yorker Rock- und Soul-Ausnahmekünstlerin ihr explosives neues Album „Running Wild“
candidateAudit.text: Sari Schorr kehrt nach Europa zurück – und sie kommt nicht leise. In diesem Herbst bringt die New Yorker Rock- und Soul-Ausnahmekünstlerin ihr explosives neues Album „Running Wild“ auf die europäischen Bühnen. Die umfangreiche Tournee steht für kompromisslose Songs, ungefilterte Energie und jene mitreißenden Auftritte, die Schorr zu einer der eindrucksvollsten Live-Künstlerinnen unserer Zeit gemacht haben. Die Tournee beginnt am 29. September mit der offiziellen „Running Wild“-Album-Release-Show im The Lexington in London. Anschließend führt sie durch Deutschland, Belgien, die Niederlande, Tschechien, Dänemark, Schweden, Norwegen, Finnland, Österreich, die Schweiz und weitere europäische Länder. „Running Wild“ erscheint im Oktober über Artone Label Group/Provogue Records und markiert sowohl ein prägendes neues Kapitel als auch einen bedeutenden Meilenstein in Schorrs Karriere. Mit ihrer Verpflichtung bei Provogue reiht sie sich in einen renommierten Künstlerkatalog ein, zu dem Namen wie Joe Bonamassa, Beth Hart und Walter Trout gehören. Das international angesehene Label ist dafür bekannt, kraftvolle, gitarrengetriebene Musik zu fördern, und bietet damit die ideale Heimat für den kühnen, weitläufigen Sound von „Running Wild“. Angetrieben von druckvollen Gitarren, donnernden Rhythmen und Schorrs unverwechselbarer Stimme schöpft „Running Wild“ aus dem ungezähmten Geist des Rock und Soul der 1970er-Jahre und führt ihn entschlossen in die Gegenwart. Die zehn selbst geschriebenen Songs erzählen von Besessenheit, Freiheit, Widerstandskraft und persönlicher Veränderung – mit große

candidateAudit.text: Three years, many seasons, countless blunzn. A small tribute to one of our longest-running menu residents. Since opening our doors, blood sausage has been one of those things that somehow never quite left the menu. It has changed with the seasons, found different companions and taken on a few different forms, but has always managed to find its way back to the plate. More often than not, crisped up and served with seasonal fruit and a rather delicious sauce. Occasionally, tucked into an equally delicious onion. So here it is, a little collection of its many lives at Centrala 🐈‍⬛

candidateAudit.title: Liebe Gäste, Fans und Freunde des Schweizerhauses! Gemeinsam Gutes bewirken durch Unterstützung für den Lichtblickhof Mit dem Ende der Saison verbinden wir im Schweizerhaus nicht n
candidateAudit.text: Liebe Gäste, Fans und Freunde des Schweizerhauses! Gemeinsam Gutes bewirken durch Unterstützung für den Lichtblickhof Mit dem Ende der Saison verbinden wir im Schweizerhaus nicht nur Dankbarkeit für viele schöne Begegnungen mit unseren Gästen, sondern auch das Bewusstsein, Verantwortung für Kinder und Ihre Familien zu übernehmen, die Unterstützung besonders dringend benötigen. Anlässlich des Saisonabschlusses am 31.10. sammelte das Schweizerhaus im Rahmen einer gemeinsamen Spendenaktion 3.550 Euro zugunsten des Kinderhospizes Lichtblickhof. Die Spendensumme entstand durch das Zusammenspiel mehrerer Initiativen: ✨ Spendenbox unseres Service-Teams ✨ Spende unseres Küchenleiters anlässlich seines 50. Geburtstages ✨ Verdoppelung des gesammelten Betrags durch die Familie Karl Kolarik Gemeinsam konnte so ein wertvoller Beitrag für den Lichtblickhof geleistet werden. Die Spende wurde an unseren langjährigen Stammgast Ing. Georg Mayrhofer ("Wiesenschurli"), engagierter Botschafter des Lichtblickhofs, übergeben. Seit vielen Jahren setzt er sich mit unermüdlichem persönlichen Einsatz für die wertvolle Arbeit des Vereins ein und sammelt Spenden. Der Lichtblickhof ist ein besonderer Ort für Familien aus ganz Österreich, deren Kind von einer unheilbaren oder lebensverkürzenden Erkrankung betroffen ist. Mit einem multiprofessionellen Therapeutinnen- und Therapeutenteam sowie speziell ausgebildeten Therapie-Tieren begleitet der gemeinnützige Verein Kinder und ihre Angehörigen durch schwere Lebensphasen. Für das Schweizerhaus-Team und die Familie Karl Kolarik ist es eine Herzensangelegenhe

candidateAudit.text: Wenn zwei, denen guter Geschmack und Lebensmittelrettung am Herzen liegen, an einem Strang ziehen: Unsere Kooperation mit genusskoarl ! 🤝🌱 Unsere gemeinsame Geschichte reicht im Grunde schon zurück bis zur Sendung “2 Minuten 2 Millionen.” Beide Betriebe sind angetreten, um zu beweisen, dass Kulinarik, Nachhaltigkeit und Innovation Hand in Hand gehen können. Umso schöner ist es, diesen Weg nun gemeinsam zu gehen: passend zum 10-jährigen Jubiläum von Genusskoarl! 🎉 Was uns verbindet, ist mehr als nur ein professionelles Miteinander: ✨ Gleiche Werte: Tiefe Wertschätzung für Menschen, Ressourcen und wertvolle Lebensmittel. ✨ Regionalität & Qualität: Der Fokus auf erstklassige heimische Zutaten und kompromisslose Standards. ✨ Neugier: Der Mut, neue Wege in der Produktentwicklung zu gehen und Altes neu zu denken. Seit 2023 ist Genusskoarl unser verlässlicher Produktionspartner. Begonnen hat alles mit unserer Tomaten Bruschetta, gefolgt von feinstem Bio Mohn Miso. Bei jedem einzelnen Produktionsschritt spürt man die enorme Sorgfalt, das handwerkliche Know-how und den hohen Qualitätsanspruch des gesamten Teams. Eine Zusammenarbeit auf Augenhöhe, die einfach Spaß macht und zeigt, was möglich ist, wenn die Chemie stimmt. Auf viele weitere Jahre partnerschaftliches Schaffen gegen die Verschwendung und für puren Genuss! 🥂

candidateAudit.text: Atomic Rooster, one of the most influential British progressive hard rock bands of the 1970s, are back with their first studio album in 43 years. Since their successful return in 2016, Atomic Rooster have built a strong reputation for outstanding live performances, consistently drawing enthusiastic crowds and delivering high-energy shows across the UK and Europe.

candidateAudit.text: What world are we building as future ancestors? How can the artifacts we leave behind tell the stories of our wildest dreams about climate justice? What is there to do then but speculate – and fight – for alternative futures and timelines? 🌳🌳🌳 Please register for this workshop via mail to: ail@uni-ak.ac.at The workshop is both a meditation on time and endurance and a hands-on workshop on what we leave behind as we lurch towards the future. There will be a short discussion to frame the session led by the artist followed by a materials workshop where we’ll get to work with our hands and practice collective speculation. General material for the workshop is provided, but you are free to bring children’s clay, coloring materials, bond paper, hand ties, ribbons, sticks or similar. In many human cosmologies, time is a grand circle, eternally cycling between the past, present, and future. In others, time is an arc, a narrative plot that marches from a momentous beginning towards an apocalyptic end. In the Filipino view, meanwhile, time is perpetually attached to human flourishing. Turning time on its head, climate injustice exists in its own temporal plane. In making sense of climate-related loss, time flows backwards, forward, and back again. Sins in the past committed through the collusion of corrupt political dynasties and the fossil fuel industry endanger the unwritten futures of young people and the variety of presents outside the struggle otherwise available for many climate activists. candidateAudit.title: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. The climate crisis is our omni-present companion these days, why not take it o
candidateAudit.text: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. The climate crisis is our omni-present companion these days, why not take it on a walk? Inspired by the deconstruction of soil caused by drought, the work ‘chainmail’ was made to make the literal weight of climate change on our shoulders something we can physically experience. This ‘fashion’ piece is meant to be worn throughout the visit of this ­exhibition, inviting the visitors to reflect on their own actions and feelings concerning the climate crisis: What is my purpose in this? How do I work through my feelings? What makes me feel better? What can I do to make the world a better place? At the end of the visit, the weight is taken off as a ­symbolic act of katharsis. Contribution by: Johanna Unterpertinger At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna running till 6 Nov 2026 Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Photos: Hannah Mayr

candidateAudit.text: Save the date! Next exhibition opening is coming up: 18 Nov, 18:00 With contributions by: adO/Aptive, Beatrice Tulagan, Eline Benjaminsen, Elias Kimaiyo, Forensic Architecture, Jonas Staal, Paolo Cirio, Prin Rodriguez, Radha D’Souza, Valentino Skarwan Opening program: Sound performance by Rudi Gier gmorrk (live set) and Oko Oko a.made.up.reality (DJ Set) The engagement with climate justice reveals a complex field of perspectives across multiple temporalities, geographies, and forms of knowledge. In this context, environmental destruction is entangled with economic interests, the uneven distribution of risks and responsibilities, colonial continuities, imperialist power relations, and geological deep time. The exhibition ’Future on Trial. Between Unruly Evidence and Unfinished Climate Justice’ moves between two conceptions of justice. One that is produced and negotiated in courtrooms through scientific and legal evidence, data, and visual investigations, and another that understands justice as an unfinished, collective process, grounded in Indigenous knowledge, queer ecology, multispecies perspectives, and activism. Through a dialogue between artistic practices and scientific experts in the field of climate litigation, the exhibition opens up a space between evidence and uncertainty, accusation and repair, institutional accountability and collective imagination. Curators: Adriano Vinca, Camille Belmin, Elisabeth Falkensteiner Expert and scientific support: Inga Menke, Joy Reyes, Krishna Ariola, Michaela Krömer, Nicholas Petkov With support from the European Geoscience Union,

candidateAudit.text: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. Mainly painted with self-made colours from soil and plant pigments, ‘Entangled’ pictures an underground view of root and ­mycelium structures. Inspired by minirhizotrones (scientific instruments to observe roots and their interactions with soil, mycelium and microorganisms over time), it offers an immersive experience of the hidden world beneath our feet while emphasising our profound connection with soil as the foundation of life, providing nutrients and supporting ecosystems. By inviting us to reflect on the entanglement of healthy soil and human well being in times of severe drought caused by human-made climate change, it opens a deeper understanding of us being part of more-than-human nature. The work ’Veins’ is inspired by the colorful digital maps of Root Image Analysis Software, which scientists use to trace and examine root networks from minirhizotron imagery. The embroidery of roots in red colour intentionally mirrors human vascular systems. This visual bridge shows the deep relation of human bodies and soil bodies, and reminds us that our survival and wellbeing is ­directly connected to healthy soil. The delicate chiffon acts as a metaphor for the fragile threshold between the above-ground world and the underground ecosystem. Referring to ‘Entangled’, ‘Veins’ steps into the lens of digital root scans – transforming scientific data into a poetic testament of more-than-human entanglements. candidateAudit.title: Next round of AIL Ping-Pong – an intervention at Counter 13 with Christos Kyritopoulos-Ninas, Florian Sorgo, Felix Helmut Wagner, Agnes Varnai In its fourth edition, AIL Ping-Pong
candidateAudit.text: Next round of AIL Ping-Pong – an intervention at Counter 13 with Christos Kyritopoulos-Ninas, Florian Sorgo, Felix Helmut Wagner, Agnes Varnai In its fourth edition, AIL Ping-Pong circles around the term and meaning of ‘blob.’ In Computer Science and Technology BLOB stands for a ‘Binary Large Object’ and is a collection of raw binary data stored as a single object. In biology, the term blob refers to a specific type of fungus consisting of a single, enormous cell. It has no brain, yet it can still learn, solve problems, and move. A blob is a form without fixed contours. It defies clear categorization: it grows, melts, merges, engulfs, and mutates. Something between body and mass, organism and data packet, slime trail and digital artifact. It can appear soft and funny – or threatening, viral, uncontrollable. Presented in the small vitrine of the Otto Wagner Postsparkasse, four graduates of the University of Applied Arts Vienna open a window into their diverse artistic practices, offering a range of perspectives that explore parallels, contrasts, or extensions within the given thematic framework AIL, Otto Wagner Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna agnes_varnai felixhelmutwagner chris_ckrtn flo_vago Photo: Agnes Varnai

candidateAudit.text: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. ’The Experiment’ is both deconstruction and reconstruction of a field experiment run by researchers at the University of Innsbruck, which simulates summer drought in a mountain grassland. Open for visitors to enter, the installation dismantles scientific processes and transforms a fictitious laboratory setting into an immersive environment, where the material traces of experimentation and data collection can be engaged with. The observer – both inside and outside of the­ ­transparent sheltered space – is invited to reflect on the nature of exploration, (drought) memory and the construction of reality. Contribution by: Michael Bahn, Konstantina Maria Serjannis At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. candidateAudit.text: Please note: Symposium starts already at 15:00✌️What are the terms under which media acts through lore, noise, sense, and air? With its second instalment, the ‘In Terms of Media…’ symposium continues the Weibel Institute for Digital Culture's ongoing engagement with contemporary media technologies. Our present is shaped not only by visible architectures of data and computation, but also by registers that precede or exceed explicit discourse: 🧶 the mythological and occult substrates through which technological imaginaries take hold; 🧶 the noise from which systems, meanings, and exclusions emerge; 🧶 the conditions of mediated life and their entanglement with colonial histories of power and sensing; 🧶 the atmospheric environments that orient conduct and produce consent without explicit command. Across four panels and one workshop, the symposium brings together artists, theorists, and practitioners to trace these registers from multiple angles, attending to the historical conditions from which our present has emerged and the alternative practices it might yet generate. With: Elisa Balmaceda, Josephine Berry, Anna Engelhardt, Sonia de Jager, Miguel Prado Casanova, Patricia Reed, Aura Satz, Valentina Tanni, Jamieson Webster, Günseli Yalcinkaya, Gary Zhexi Zhang, and Jesse Damiani Presented by The Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures. The symposium will be held in English

candidateAudit.text: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. Three transparent cylinders reveal the hidden layers of soil as it is exposed to increasing levels of dryness. As experimental drought progresses over the course of the exhibition, the structure and appearance of the soil changes. Visible traces like cracks, compaction, and disintegration reflect the gradient of water supply and –scarcity in the three vessels. The installation Drought Traces points to the fragile balance between water, soil and life. Drought Traces. Contribution by: Michael Bahn, Cornelia Dirnberger, Christian Prohammer At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. candidateAudit.title: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. Hands touch, intervene, secure traces, expose. Cutting, tearing, rubbing. Soil
candidateAudit.text: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. Hands touch, intervene, secure traces, expose. Cutting, tearing, rubbing. Soil is both experimental surface and site of action. Distance between body and ground, the disposable latex glove as a separating membrane. As a symbol of experiment and intervention, the glove marks the moment of active intervention; the motif evokes experimental setups in the field, laboratory situations in situ, and, at the same time, forensic investigation. Through exposing, drilling, and excavating, the ground becomes a site of ambivalent human-environment relations: between proximity and separation, intervention and restraint. The Tat-Ort is a locus of forensic ethnography, where observation and analysis intersect with remnants of violation and evidence collection. The installation assembles fragments of an artistic research process – notes, materials, objects, traces – on soil and drought. On the table, the act of investigation becomes visible: the laboratory table transforms into both a site of knowledge production and a scene of evidence. [Exhibit B] hands on – hands off [Exhibit A] Am Tat-Ort: ­Evidence on the Laboratory Table Contributions by: Konstantina Maria Serjannis At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. candidateAudit.text: Save the date and register for this workshop 🌐 We live in a highly globalised and hyper-connected world. At the same time, it feels like falling apart: To a large extent, we have lost connection – to ‘others’ in society, to ‘other’ kinds of knowing, and to something we are used to call ‘nature’. What really matters to us? Is it possible to un-learn and un-do ingrained habits or routines resulting in ways of living severely threatening ecosystems and resulting in multiple socio-ecological crises we are facing nowadays? Out of a sense of urgency, can a mindset emerge that entails a more-than-human way of thinking and acting, both individually and collectively? Workshop with Franziska Allerberger. Duration: 13:15–15:30 Please register for this workshop via link in bio! (free entry) The workshop is an invitation to explore these questions and themes by getting in motion through a performative and embodied approach. In doing so, we also reflect upon the creative potential of art-science collaborations (such as 03: Soil) for unleashing societal change towards a healthier future on Planet Earth. Franziska Allerberger is a geographer and pursues a training in theater pedagogy. She is interested in interfaces of science, arts, policy and civil society, and how collaborations between these distinct actor groups can be facilitated and strengthened to contribute to a livable future. Her geographic perspective is the starting point for her artistic explorations at AIL. Part of the exhibition ‘03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’

At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. candidateAudit.title: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive na
candidateAudit.text: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive narrative obscures a deeper, more ‘errant’ truth? Media theorist and author Clemens Apprich in conversation with philosopher Jan Völker. Moderated by Amanda Holmes, Department of Philosophy, University of Applied Arts Vienna Welcome: Ulrike Kuch, Rector of the University of Applied Arts Vienna A cooperation of the department of Media Theory and the department of Philosophy. ‘Errant Intelligence’ challenges the prevailing biological and individualistic interpretations of machine learning, arguing instead for a radical understanding of machine intelligence. The book embraces the deviations, inconsistencies, and ‘errant behaviour’ as fundamental to the discovery of new knowledge, moving beyond the illusion of mere optimisation. Drawing on media theory, cybernetics, and a unique psychoanalytic lens, it explores the ‘technological unconscious’ of machine learning. It traces the historical roots of AI, from early automatons and the Turing machine to natural language processing and contemporary machine learning systems. Challenging the idea of an autonomous, self-generating AI, the book exposes the hidden labour, assumed logics, and inherent biases that animate its operation. It re-evaluates computational thinking, insisting on its inherently social, collective, and symbolic character, and revealing how language and logical paradoxes are not obstacles but constitutive forces that shape intelligent machines

candidateAudit.text: Eigentlich sollte sie nur ein Test sein. Unsere Pizza Maroni war zuerst nicht auf der Karte. candidateAudit.title: In this workshop with Helena Detsch we will explore simple ways to create a fascinating natural color palette from soil and plant-based materials like earths, minerals, vegetables,
candidateAudit.text: In this workshop with Helena Detsch we will explore simple ways to create a fascinating natural color palette from soil and plant-based materials like earths, minerals, vegetables, kitchen supplies and algae pigments. Part of the exhibition ‘03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ Duration: 15:30–17:30 Please register for this workshop via link in bio (free entry) Together, we'll first experiment with making self-made oil- or watercolors from 100% natural sources and then explore the many possibilities of sustainable painting, discovering how these self-made colors behave on paper and fabric and what a truly organic painting practice can look like. In her oil paintings, installations and animations, Helena Detsch explores (mis-)relationships between humans and more-than-human life. Her series and immersive spatial installations question Western anthropocentric narratives about nature as a resource and create spaces to reflect on coexistence and complex interconnections between human and other agents. To develop a more sustainable art practice, she crafts natural colors from plant and soil pigments. helena.kettu AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna dieangewandte

candidateAudit.text: Coming up next as part of VIENNA DESIGN WEEK 2026 🪢 The exhibition ’Zero and One Chairs’ was created as part of MATCH!, a recurring initiative organised by the department of Applied Photography and Time-Based Media at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, which explores the synergistic potential of student teams from different degree programs. In collaboration with the department Industrial Design, this year’s focus was on the intersection of photography and the object, with particular attention paid to the relationship with set design, styling, casting and narrative. Seen from the perspective of Applied Photography, the object and thus the chair, is a welcome protagonist. Photography’s multiple applied genres are cited here: documentary, fashion, advertising, architecture and the portrait. When the function in Industrial Design coalesces with the idea of the purpose in Applied Photography, the question of factuality emerges. Be not mistaken: The most literal things are often the most confusing and enigmatic. Between what it is and how it is*, worlds unfold. We put the images to work. candidateAudit.text: Throughout August and September, the artist duo MUELLER-DIVJAK is residing at AIL for Summer Studio – using the space for artistic research, experimentation, and learning, developing the project's multisensory scenography – the so-called SΫS SPACE. Aim of the Summer Studio is to prepare the prototype of the scenography, which will be established at the AIL in June 2027 as the centerpiece of the final exhibition of the PEEK project ’SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS — Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenography for Systems Awareness.’ The SΫS SPACE facilitates a physical experience of one's own embededdness within living systems, within complex interrelationships – within a greater whole. It paves the way for relational sensing and thinking – an embodied systems awareness, that can help in coping with complexity, challenges, and uncertainties, and in making good decisions towards sustainable futures. It deliberately reduces the dominance of the sense of sight, placing the emphasis instead on smell, touch, and hearing. Numerous scientists, as well as invited artists, politicians, journalists, children, senior citizens, curators, cultural workers, educators, and teenagers are individually guided through the immersive environment by Jeanette Müller and Paul Divjak and share their responses in photo-based reflections and semi-structured interviews. Their feedback directly informs the prototype. Save the date! 14 and 15 Sep 2026 The SΫS SPACE will open to the public in individual time slots for an exclusive multisensory experience.
